Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Pinnacle Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the operator instructions are to queue up using the star key followed by one on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Pinnacle Asset Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Investment Officer; Laura Bennett, Head of Distribution; David Kwon, Head of Operations; Rachel Patel, Head of Risk Management; and Kevin Singh, Head of Technology.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust net inflows, positive market appreciation, and strong client retention across our global franchise. Our AUM grew to a record $1.25 trillion.

Emily Chen: Thank you, Johnathan. From a financial perspective, Pinnacle Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $850 million, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher fee-related earnings from expanded AUM and performance fee realizations. Our expenses were $458 million, resulting in net income of $250 million. Our expense ratio improved to 22 basis points due to operating leverage from scale and efficiencies in technology and shared services.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we dive into our financial results, I'd like to start with our core metric: Assets Under Management, or AUM. Ending AUM reached $1.25 trillion, reflecting an 18% year-over-year increase and a sequential 5% quarter-over-quarter growth. This was powered by strong net inflows of $45 billion—our highest in two years—positive market appreciation from the S&P 500's 8% rally and global equity rebound, plus about 3% organic growth from client retention and wallet share gains.

Breaking this down by geography highlights our diversified global footprint, now with 60% of AUM managed across regions, up from 52% last year. North America, at 55% or $687.5 billion, grew 16% year-over-year with $28 billion in net inflows, driven by institutional demand for our low-cost ETF suite like the Pinnacle Core Equity ETF mirroring the Russell 3000, which hit $15 billion AUM. Retirement platforms such as Vanguard and Fidelity boosted target-date funds amid rising 401(k) contributions, while U.S. tech tailwinds from the Magnificent Seven added $12 billion. We're expanding into private markets with a new evergreen infrastructure fund at $5 billion targeting data centers and renewables for the AI boom.

Europe, 25% or $312.5 billion, rose 22% year-over-year with €18 billion inflows. The EU's SFDR favored our Article 8 and 9 ESG strategies like the Pinnacle Euro Sustainable Bond Fund, drawing €10 billion from Dutch pensions like APG. Strength in the UK and Nordics came from our AI-driven quant strategies returning 12% gross versus MSCI Europe's 6%, aided by ECB cuts. We're growing our UCITS platform with two new active ETFs for European small-caps, eyeing €20 billion by year-end.

Asia-Pacific, 15% or $187.5 billion, surged 28% with $12 billion inflows. China QFII expansions brought $4 billion to our Greater China Equity Fund on CSI 300 recovery; India added $3 billion via private wealth like Kotak Mahindra amid Nifty highs. Japan yen-hedged strategies won GPIF mandates. Our HSBC blockchain custody cut settlement times 40%, unlocking $2 billion in tokenized alts. With Asia's $25 trillion wealth transfer by 2030, we're investing $500 million in local hires and localization for 20% growth in FY25.

Rest of World, 5% or $62.5 billion, grew 12% with $5 billion inflows from Gulf SWFs like ADIA into our $10 billion Global Direct Lending Fund, plus Brazil pension demand for inflation-linked assets.

Organic AUM growth excluding markets was 8%, beating peers, with flows into ETFs (55%) and alts (25%), ESG at 18%. Our Global Alpha 3.0 machine learning for allocation lifted returns 150 bps in tests. M&A pipeline targets $10-15 billion Asia boutiques; five new interval funds for U.S. RIAs aim for 12-15% AUM CAGR.

On AUM by asset class, ending at $1.28 trillion adjusted for consistency, QoQ growth was 4.2%, YoY 16.7%, from $28 billion inflows, $32 billion markets, $2 billion FX. Equities at 46% ($589 billion) grew QoQ 6.1%, YoY 22.4% on AI tech beta and $15 billion inflows. Fixed income at 28% ($358 billion) up QoQ 1.8%, YoY 9.2% via corporates and ABS. Alternatives at 22% ($282 billion) surged QoQ 7.3%, YoY 28.6%, private credit at $127 billion yielding 10.2%, new interval funds $3.5 billion. Organic 3.1% QoQ. Scaling alts to 25%, active ETFs, APAC hub.

Operating expenses totaled $458 million, up 4.2% YoY but flat sequentially, expense ratio 22 bps from $1.2 trillion AUM leverage. Compensation $252 million (55%), up 6% on headcount to 4,200, variable comp from alts. Tech/data $68 million (15%), up 12% for Apex Sentinel ESG integration, cybersecurity, gen-AI. G&A $72 million (16%), down 2% on hybrid work, RPA. Marketing/distribution $42 million (9%), up 8% for sub-advisory, APAC JV. Amortization/other $24 million flat. OpEx/revenue 68%, margins 32%. FY24 guide $1.85-1.90 billion.

Performance fees hit $178 million in Q3, up 32% YoY, TTM $612 million. From equity long/short like Vertex Equity Partners $1.1 billion gains, private equity exits. 22% revenue mix. Equities 8.2% gross vs. S&P 500 7.1%, net 7.5%; fixed 3.1% vs. Agg 2.4%; alts 5.6% vs. HFRI 3.9%. Quant ML, ESG top-quartile. Q4 $200 million expected.

Net flows $18.7 billion: institutional $9.2 billion (LDI, ETFs), retail $6.1 billion (dividend ETF, direct indexing), alts $3.4 billion (credit, infra). Organic 6.2%.

Capital allocation: $4.5 billion cash, 1.2x leverage. Organic $2.1 billion (alts, ETFs), inorganic $1.4 billion (Summit $120 billion alts, quant tuck-ins), tech $700 million (AI, blockchain), returns $450 million buybacks/dividends. FY24 $4.5-5 billion.

M&A: Acquired Horizon Alternatives $650 million ($18 billion alts), EuroBeta ETFs €1.1 billion (€12 billion). Synergies realized, pipeline active.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Emily. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by dynamically allocating via machine learning models that integrate alternative data like satellite imagery, enhancing stock selection and outperformance by 25 bps in equities. We launched the Pinnacle Core Equity ETF this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $15 billion AUM and strong institutional adoption.

Laura Bennett: Thank you, Michael. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in EMEA and APAC are paying off, as evidenced by $22.1 billion EMEA and $13.1 billion APAC flows.

Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning, everyone. On our client franchise, we hit 95.2% annual retention, up to 98.1% asset retention, beating benchmarks. Alpha generation, AlphaEdge AI platform drove NPS to 78. Cross-sell to 2.8 products, $42 billion retention inflows. New acquisition $92.7 billion YTD, institutional $51 billion, intermediary $32 billion, HNWI $9.7 billion. Client360 CRM boosted conversion 18%. Q1'24 interval funds, EdgeWealth robo $12 billion. FY24 guide $85-100 billion.

David Kwon: Thank you, Laura. Operationally, we've made significant progress in streamlining our middle and back office functions via RPA and cloud migrations. This has resulted in increased efficiency, 20% infrastructure savings, and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on regulatory compliance enhancements for SFDR and Dodd-Frank.

Rachel Patel: Thank you, David. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and geopolitical risks, stress-testing VaR against rate shocks keeping drawdowns low. This includes integrating real-time ESG data and net-zero models into AlphaForge.

Kevin Singh: Thank you, Rachel. On the technology front, we are investing in advanced analytics and AI to enhance our investment decision-making process and improve client service, including NLP on earnings transcripts for 150 bps equity edge and blockchain for custody. We are also focused on strengthening our cybersecurity posture with quantum-resistant tools. Specifically, Apex Sentinel now covers 85% AUM, Client360 predicts switches at 87% accuracy, and Tech 2026 roadmap allocates $200 million for tokenization.

Johnathan Hale: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities like Global Alpha 3.0 and M&A, and capitalizing on alternatives and ETF opportunities ahead.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from David Lee with Morningstar.

David Lee: Good morning. Can you provide more details on client retention and new client acquisition strategies?

Johnathan Hale: Thanks, David. Our 95.2% retention reflects alpha outperformance by 210 bps net in equities and low volatility in fixed income. Client360 and OCIO growth to $18 billion are key. New wins like $4.2 billion DC mandate show RFP strength, guiding $85-100 billion FY24 inflows.

David Lee: Thank you. And a follow-up on operating expenses breakdown?

Emily Chen: Sure. Comp up on alts realizations, tech for Sentinel and AI, G&A down via hybrid, marketing for retail. Margins to 32%, guiding 5% growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Bloomberg.

Sarah Kim: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Pinnacle Core Equity ETF?

Michael Torres: Absolutely. PCORE tracked Russell 3000 tightly with low tracking error, inflows $15 billion from retirement platforms. Overweights in tech drove excess returns amid Nasdaq gains.

Sarah Kim: And how is the new alternatives interval fund performing relative to expectations?

Laura Bennett: Exceeding with $3.5 billion inflows, 9-11% IRRs in private credit, monthly liquidity appealing to RIAs and HNWIs.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Patel: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

David Kwon: We've automated 90% SFDR reporting, RPA for reconciliation saving $20 million annually, hybrid utilization at 60%, all dropping cost-to-income below 35%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan.

Lisa Chen: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Rachel Patel: SFDR and SEC rules are tailwinds for ESG, which is 18% AUM. Our Sentinel platform automates compliance, reducing costs 25%, with VaR models mitigating election and China risks.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Hayes with Barclays.

Robert Hayes: How are you leveraging technology to improve investment performance?

Kevin Singh: AI sentiment from 10 million transcripts, alt data for 150 bps edge, HorizonOne covering 85% AUM with 3x ROI on launches, blockchain unlocking tokenized alts.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Pinnacle Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
